Mechanical alloying was carried out at room temperature in a planetary ball-milling machine (QM-BP) with stainless steel cell and bearing steel balls. The cell was loaded with mixture of Nb (99.9 wt%, /C0 200 meshes) and W (99.8 wt%, /C0 250 meshes) powders together with 500 g balls. The powders were blended in appropriate amounts to give the nominal composition of Nb– XW (X¼10, 20, 30 wt%). Absolute ethyl alcohol was used as process control agents (PCA) during milling. During milling, the ball to powder weight ratio, solid to liquid ratio, milling time and rotation speed were maintained at 6:1, 1:0.2, 12 h and 250 rpm [29], respectively.
Milled powders were screened and dried for 20 h at temperature of 90 1C in vacuum drying chest.
The powders were loaded into high-strength graphite mould shown in Fig. 1 and cold-pressed with pressures of 10 MPa at room temperature

The mould was ﬁrstly raised to 1200 1C using a heating rate of 25 1C/min and kept 5 min, followed to 1800 1C using a heating rate of 20 1C/min and kept 90 min under 30 MPa, and then furnace cooled to ambient temperature.

However, 20 W and 30 W alloys exhibited the better oxidation resistance due to the denser oxides scale though the ﬁne granular oxides grew into coarse columnar, as shown in Fig. 7e and f.

W addition to Nb gives rise to an increase in room temperature ﬂexural strength due to solid solution strengthening, but W content must meet or even exceed 30% which can efﬁciently strengthen the alloy.

Fracture toughness ﬁrst increases obviously and then decreases slightly with W changing from 10% to 30%, which was attributed to ductile fracture propensity in 20 W alloy and remarkable solid solution strengthening in 30 W alloy, respectively.
